questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Career opportunities

questions.question: Please explain: *
Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Relevance of the area - since I study area studies, it was important to me to choose a relevant area. Also, the aspect of the courses available was important.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was easy as we had orientation days as well as we received several e-mails with information in advance.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: We had orientation days, as well as the fact that a group of Erasmus people were there to help us.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: I lived in the student hostel, however, it was open for all, therefore I am not sure if it is, in fact, a real part of the campus, but it was however still connected to the University to some extend, as we lived together in dorms with other university students at the host university.

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: Kitchen with almost everything included, except from oven.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer: It is very enriching as you get to live together and socialize with fellow students. Also, the facilities are usually fine and student friendly.

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: You arrived, registered to courses if you had not already done it (in around the first two weeks you could change courses) then you participated in orientation days and afterwards signed documents.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: The staff at the host university, Erasmus staff, as well as the staff from the home university to help in guiding.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Successful. At first, some of the courses for which I had gotten a pre-approval were not there, however, I ended up finding some other courses very interesting as well, therefore, there was no problem.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Read documents carefully - participate in any orientation meetings and days - not to hesitate to use the help available to you (host institution, home institution, Erasmus staff ect.)

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: Both

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: One MA course were a bit difficult, or maybe it was more the way it was built that was different from what I have been used to at UCPH, however, the others courses were not as difficult, though, still challenging and I gained many new competencies and new knowledge.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: As mentioned earlier, some courses were different from what used to. The one course being quite different had some more "practical" aspects in it, including a simulation exercise. Also, the courses were built upon work throughout the semester instead of one single exam that you are graded upon. Here, you had assignments, work-shops ect. which were a part of the final grade.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:

The Baltic Sea Region in International System (SORG.04.015)

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your second semester. *
What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: EU - Russia Relations if you are interested in politics or are studying area studies or likely as this was a very enriching course.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Running club, several cultural and social events such as movie night, Estonian cultural evening, karaoke night ect.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Running club. I did not do this myself, however, I heard very good about it. Also, participate in some of the cultural events.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Visit other interesting cities in the country, visit local museums, explore unique places of the city and similar.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It was alright as I have already been traveling quite much in the region, as well as been on summer school in the same country before.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Be friendly, be interested in learning about their culture as well as respecting their culture. Also, just be yourself, it may sound cliché but it is nevertheless true. If you are just yourself as well as kind and respectful, people are usually more open than we may think.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Not really so many as I knew them already.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The friendliness and the helpfulness.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Remember to go to classes. You learn a lot, not least other academic ways of learning, you may be challenged by the different ways of learning but this is only good and gives you a lot of experience! Here, you should also know that the grades are a part of different tasks you do throughout the semester and not built upon one single exam at the end of the semester.

Acknowledging that you can never be completely prepared for what awaits and also knowing that many of the students you will be surrounded with are new just like you.

Take use of the many student-friendly facilities (e.g. libraries, cafés ect.) or attractions (such as several University museums, cathedral or similar) in the city as many aspects of the city is highly built upon the university.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Be curious and openminded!

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Developing my academic competencies, getting introduced to new parts of my field that could interest me as well as making close friends.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Probably one of the master courses I took as many elements were new for me.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: Exchange does not only develop your academic skills, it also develops you as a person. You gain so much experience and knowledge which will be forever useful in your future life.

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
